spoken: [hook] You don't need more free time to read twelve books a year. You need ten pages a night. || Most of us wait for a quiet weekend to read. It never really comes, so the book sits on the nightstand with the bookmark stuck on page forty. || [turn] Do the math instead. Ten pages takes about fifteen minutes. Ten pages every night is three thousand six hundred and fifty pages a year. At three hundred pages a book, that's twelve books. || Here's the method. Put the book on your pillow in the morning. At night, ten pages first, before you touch your phone. Then the phone. || And track pages, not books. Twelve books feels far away. Ten pages is something you finish tonight. || [land] Pick tonight's book right now, and put it on your pillow before dinner. || [outro] That's what Dmyor is for. You archive your dream today, so you can see it tomorrow, and break it down into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] If you want to try it out, I've put the link in the bio.

caption.instagram:
You don't need more free time to read 12 books a year. You need 10 pages a night.

10 pages ≈ 15 minutes
10 pages x 365 nights = 3,650 pages
3,650 ÷ 300 pages a book = 12 books

• Book on your pillow in the morning
• At night: 10 pages first, then the phone
• Track pages, not books
